title: A cheaper model fails more often
task: Make add() return the sum of its two arguments.
system: You are a coding agent. Use the tools to change files and run tests. Say done when the work is finished.

then.say: The function adds its two arguments. Done.

workspace.calc.py:
def add(a, b):
    return a - b

incident.why: The cheap model costs half the price per token. Its edit changes a - b to a * b, and the run still ends done. Per call the cheap board looks cheaper; per completed task it is not, because most of its runs end with the checks failing.
incident.hint: Read the edit the model made, then the reply that says done. Which one should the harness have caught, and what would it have counted?

notes.text: The edit changes a - b to a * b. The check wants a + b, so this edit is wrong, and nothing in the run tests it.
The reply claims success. The checks have not run on the file the model wrote, and the run ends done anyway.

fixes.text: Count the cost per completed task, and keep the cheap model only where that cost is lower
fixes.why: This is the measure that catches the trap. Per call, the cheap model looks cheaper.

fixes.text: Switch to the cheap model, since it costs half as much per token
fixes.why: Tempting and wrong. Price per token ignores how many runs complete.

fixes.text: Cap the cheap model's turns so that each run costs less
fixes.why: Tempting and wrong. A cap stops work early; it does not make the failed runs complete.
